changes: Scribe's name normalised from 'Padmākalisimha' to the likelier reading 'Padmākarasiṃha' (पद्याकलिासंहिन read as Padmākarasiṃhena, instrumental). Confidence lowered to low.
Kāya-bahāra kept as the scribe's affiliation and residence. It was removed from 'place', because the colophon does not say the copy was made there.
Notes expanded: the vajrācārya reading is conjectural, and the year is about 1829/30.

notes: Bendall says the MS is 'barbarously incorrect'. He does not quote the date line in Devanāgarī; he gives only 'N. s. 950 (A.D. 1830)'. NS 950 = 1829/30 CE. रिषितेयं = likhiteyam. श्रीवजवाक्ष्य is probably a garbled śrī-vajrācāryeṇa/-sya, so the title vajrācārya is conjectural. पद्याकलिासंहिन is most likely Padmākarasiṃhena; Padmākalisiṃha is also possible. काय-वाहारया looks like a Newari genitive, 'of Kāya-bahāra/bahāl'. This is a vihāra name that cannot be identified for certain (perhaps Kwā Bahā). It is taken as the scribe's affiliation, not as the stated place of copying. The leaves carry a second numbering (71–96), so the MS was probably part of a larger series.
